subject: math
title: Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations
syllabus: Complex numbers as ordered pairs of reals, Representation of complex numbers in the form a + ib and their representation in a plane, Argand diagram, algebra of complex numbers, modulus and argument (or amplitude) of a complex number, Quadratic equations in real and complex number system and their solutions. Relations between roots and coefficient, nature of roots, the formation of quadratic equations with given roots.

Statement I : For any two non-zero complex numbers z_{1}, z_{2}, (|z_{1}| + |z_{2}|)|\f{z_{1}}{|z_{1}|} + \f{z_{2}}{|z_{2}|}| ≤ 2(|z_{1}| + |z_{2}|) and Statement II : If x, y, z are three distinct complex numbers and a, b, c are three positive real numbers such that \f{a}{|y − z|} = \f{b}{|z − x|} = \f{c}{|x − y|}, then \f{a^{2}}{y − z} + \f{b^{2}}{z − x} + \f{c^{2}}{x − y} = 1.

II: a = k|y − z| → \f{a^{2}}{y − z} = k^{2}\overline{(y − z)}; the three conjugates add to 0, not 1 → false.

pyq.q: Among the statements (S1) : The set {z ∈ C − {−i} : |z| = 1 and \f{z − i}{z + i} is purely real} contains exactly two elements, and (S2) : The set {z ∈ C − {−1} : |z| = 1 and \f{z − 1}{z + 1} is purely imaginary} contains infinitely many elements.
sol: S1: the quotient is real only on the line through i and −i, which meets |z| = 1 at ±i; −i is excluded → one element. S1 false.
S2: for |z| = 1, \f{z − 1}{z + 1} = i tan\f{θ}{2} — imaginary for every such z → infinitely many. S2 true.
